evals.query: Write tests for my LoginScreen component

files.content: export function LoginScreen() { /* renders email/password fields and a Log in button */ }

expected_behavior: Runs scripts/detect_stack.sh or otherwise confirms this is an Expo MANAGED project (expo present, no ios/android folders) and that jest-expo is already configured
Asks the user a clarifying question covering both test layer and scope before generating tests
Queries by accessible role/text (getByRole, getByPlaceholderText), not by testID as a first choice

evals.query: Add tests for the CartBadge component, it reads from our Zustand cart store
expected_behavior: Identifies this as a plain React Native CLI project (no expo dependency) and uses the react-native Jest preset, not jest-expo
Identifies Zustand as the state-management library and exercises the real store, resetting state via useCartStore.setState(useCartStore.getInitialState()) rather than mocking the store
Does NOT automatically run the tests or the fault-injection self-check -- only asked to add tests

evals.query: Test my app/profile/[id].tsx route -- it should show a 'not found' state for an unknown id

files.content: export default function ProfileRoute() { /* reads id param, renders profile or not-found state */ }

expected_behavior: Detects expo-router is present and treats this as a route-level test, not a plain component render
Uses renderRouter from expo-router/testing-library with an initialUrl matching the route under test, per reference/expo-router-testing.md
Places the new test file in __tests__/ or a sibling directory, explicitly NOT inside app/ itself, since expo-router treats every file there as a route
Covers both the found-profile case and the not-found case as the user requested

evals.query: Add tests for the copyShareLink function and run them to verify they actually catch bugs

files.content:
import * as Clipboard from 'expo-clipboard';
export async function copyShareLink(link) { if (!link) throw new Error('link required'); await Clipboard.setStringAsync(link); }

expected_behavior: Recognizes 'run them to verify they actually catch bugs' as an explicit request for verification and proceeds through Step 7 without a separate confirmation round-trip
Mocks expo-clipboard at the module boundary and asserts the delegation (setStringAsync called with the right argument), per reference/native-module-mocking.md
Actually runs the generated tests and confirms they pass against the real implementation
Runs the fault-injection self-check from reference/verification.md: introduces a deliberate fault, confirms the test goes red, then reverts it to its exact original state
